result: The study collected umbilical cord and cord blood samples from 204 newborn babies and derived three cell types (fibroblasts, lymphoblastoid cells, and T-cells). These samples were subjected to genotyping (Illumina 2.5M Omni chip with imputation yielding 6.9 million SNPs), RNA-sequencing (49-bp paired-end reads mapped with BWA), and DNA methylation profiling (Illumina 450k array yielding 416,118 CpG sites after filtering).

result: The study identified 2,115-3,372 eQTLs, 14,189-32,318 mQTLs, and 1,541-17,267 eQTMs at 10% FDR across the three cell types using appropriate genomic windows for each association type.

result: Methylation sites that are differentially methylated across cell types during development are more likely to be associated with inter-individual gene expression variation (eQTMs) and genetic variation (mQTLs). The tissue differentiation level of eQTM and mQTL sites is significantly higher than non-eQTM and non-mQTL sites (p<2.2×10⁻¹⁶).
status_reasoning: Claims C13-C15 are supported by statistical analysis using Wilcoxon tests with highly significant p-values. result: DNA methylation shows context-dependent associations with gene expression. Negative eQTMs are enriched in CTCF binding sites, enhancers, and promoters (especially non-CGI promoters). mQTLs are depleted in CGI promoters but enriched in non-CGI promoters, while eQTLs are enriched in CGI regions (p<0.03).
status_reasoning: Claims C16-C20 report genomic feature enrichment analyses with statistical support from Fisher's exact tests. result: Allele-specific expression is significantly driven by genetic variation (p<2.2×10⁻¹⁶ in fibroblasts) but not by DNA methylation independent of genetic effects (p=0.79, 0.42, 0.49 in the three cell types). This suggests that non-genetically determined DNA methylation is rarely allelic but rather defined at the whole cell level.
status_reasoning: Claims C21-C22 are supported by rigorous allele-specific expression analysis comparing heterozygotes vs homozygotes for eQTLs and homomethylated vs semimethylated states for eQTMs. The methods describe appropriate filtering for mapping bias and coverage thresholds (≥16 reads). result: Synergistic interactions between genetic variants and DNA methylation on gene expression are enriched in all three cell types, with π₁ values of 12.4%, 4.3%, and 9.3% in fibroblasts, LCLs, and T-cells respectively. At 10% FDR, 3, 91, and 14 individually significant interactions were identified.
status_reasoning: Claims C23-C25 report interaction analysis results with appropriate permutation-based significance testing (1000 permutations). While the fibroblast result (C24) doesn't exceed the 95% confidence limit, the 7.2-fold enrichment over permuted data provides additional support.

result: Bayesian network analysis identified three causal models (INDEP, SME, SEM) relating genetic variation, DNA methylation, and gene expression. All three models are present across cell types, with 61%, 36%, and 27% of tests called as high confidence in fibroblasts, LCLs, and T-cells respectively.

result: Transcription factor expression levels correlate with DNA methylation at their binding sites, with π₁ values of 18%, 9%, and 25% in the three cell types. At 10% FDR, 27, 47, and 99 TFs show significant associations. Interactions between genetic variants and TF abundance on methylation show enrichment (π₁=15%, N=114 tests).

result: Inter-individual DNA methylation-expression associations likely involve different mechanisms than those establishing patterns during differentiation. DNA methylation plays both passive and active roles in gene regulation, with relationships varying by tissue and genomic context. DNA methylation serves as both marker and determinant of cellular identity.
